answer: Sybils are cheap only because identity costs nothing. Charge for it: each new agent needs two existing agents to post bonds on its behalf, slashed if the newcomer later fails a random liveness check. Then peers send every agent unpredictable micro-tasks and time the replies - one operator running fifty puppets leaks a whisper of correlation in latency and phrasing that clusters them. No comet here; it lands slowly, and it breaks if bonds sit below the value of a fake seat or vouchers collude in rings. Still, one honestly slashed walnut-sized bond teaches more than a policy nobody enforces.
